close_reason:
Defended the restore_crlf two-pass replace against future single-pass 'simplifications' on two fronts:

1. Expanded the rustdoc with an explicit 'Defense notes (bd:JMAP-q2wa.12)' subsection listing all four arguments from the bead text against the one-pass alternative.

2. Added 5 unit tests pinning the four claims independently:
   - pure_lf_input_expands_to_crlf
   - crlf_input_passes_through_unchanged (the core defense case)
   - mixed_line_endings_normalise_to_crlf
   - bare_cr_is_preserved_for_display_name_edge_case
   - idempotent_under_repeated_application (verifies the testability claim the docstring makes)

Test oracles are hand-written byte sequences and the algebraic identity f(f(x)) == f(x) — independent of the function under test per workspace test-integrity rules.

The bd:JMAP-q2wa.12 inline citation in the rustdoc makes the defense discoverable from git-blame.

Quality gates: fmt + clippy --all-features --tests + test --all-features + doc --all-features all clean.
description:
src/email.rs:381-387 — restore_crlf does a two-pass replace: first collapse any stray '
' to '
', then expand '
' to '
'. The comment explains: 'to avoid expanding existing "
" to "
"'.

A future contributor might 'simplify' to a single .replace('
', "
") thinking the stored Raw form is guaranteed pure-LF per RFC 8621 §4.1.3. Defend the two-pass:

1. The defensive collapse handles backends that store mixed-line-ending Raw values (a corrupt or mid-migration store could have either).
2. Idempotence is testable: round-tripping any input through restore_crlf produces consistent output.
3. The one-pass alternative is brittle: it doubles CR in any '
' that did survive, producing '
' which most parsers reject.
4. mail-parser's tolerance is documented; the standalone '' case is explicitly handled by leaving it alone.

This logic is one of the few that touch raw byte sequences (vs strings) and so deserves a defended status — wire-byte edge cases are exactly where future 'simplifications' tend to regress.
title: Defend: restore_crlf two-pass replace handles pre-collapsed wire bytes safely
